# Two-column explanation

Model: `two-columns`. Each call creates a complete slide. Inter, geometry and text sizes are fixed.

[Model index](../../../templates/MODELS.md) · [Palette and content guide](../../STUDIO-MODELS.md)

```latex
\studiosetup{palette=light}
\studiotemplate[variant=default]{two-columns}
```

Palette switches are available only where the original composition exists in both colours.
Unsupported explicit choices fail. A global palette leaves special compositions in their native treatment.

## Variants and named fields

### default

Original palettes: light.

[Current source](../../../templates/studio/two-columns.tex) · [Full slot guide](../guides/two-columns.md)

| Field | Default | Available space |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | <code>Slide title</code> | 50.5% wide × 8.5% high |
| `label-two` | <code>Supporting explanation</code> | 80.2% wide × 9.7% high |
| `label-three` | <code>Label 3</code> | 21.9% wide × 6.4% high |
| `label-four` | <code>Label 4</code> | 21.1% wide × 6.4% high |
| `label-five` | <code>Supporting explanation.\\Add your own details.</code> | 38.5% wide × 43.0% high |
| `label-six` | <code>Supporting explanation.\\Add your own details.</code> | 38.1% wide × 43.0% high |

Omitted fields retain these descriptive defaults; empty values retain their allocated space. Numbers and charts are illustrative.

## Complete one-slide example

```latex
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{beamer}
\usetheme{bitpolito-studio}
\usepackage{bitpolitostudiotemplates}
\usepackage[backend=biber]{biblatex}
\addbibresource{bibliography.bib}
\begin{document}
\studiotemplate[
  variant={default},
  palette={light},
  title={Slide title},
  label-two={Supporting explanation}
]{two-columns}
\end{document}
```
